title: Twitter Feed — Fanout on Write (Basic)
subtitle: Pre-compute every follower's timeline at write time

nodes.label:
Tweet Service
Validate (280 chars)
Snowflake ID gen

Fanout Worker
Fetch follower list
LPUSH to each follower

Redis Timelines
Key: timeline:{userId}
LPUSH tweetId
LTRIM 0 799

Tweet DB
MySQL sharded by userId

panels.title: API · POST /api/tweets
panels.body:
POST /api/tweets
{ "content": "Hello world!", "userId": "user123" }
→ { "tweetId": "1234567890", "createdAt": "..." }

Fanout (one LPUSH per follower):
  LPUSH timeline:follower1 1234567890
  LPUSH timeline:follower2 1234567890
  …  × N followers

panels.title: Read path (timeline fetch)
panels.body:
LRANGE timeline:123 0 99
→ [tweetId1, tweetId2, …, tweetId100]

Hydrate from Tweet DB:
  SELECT * FROM tweets WHERE id IN (...)

panels.title: Why this breaks at scale
panels.body:
Celebrity problem: @elonmusk has 100M followers
  → ONE tweet = 100M Redis LPUSH writes
  → Timeline service overwhelmed for seconds–minutes
  → Followers see delayed or missing tweets

Wasted storage: 10M inactive users still get timeline writes

Needed: hybrid fanout (see Advanced)
